CAP 4.7uF 100V X7S 1210 AEC-Q200 -55 to +125C - buck output, one of the C601 || C602 pair. TWO 1210 IN PARALLEL RATHER THAN ONE 2220: this cap sits UPSTREAM of F601 and so is not protected by it - if the LTC3639 high side switch fails short, F601 opens and leaves this node at the full pack voltage continuously, fed through R601 and L601, which is 67V at 16S. A cracked MLCC fails SHORT and would then put the pack across L601, the exact failure this part exists to prevent, so flex-crack resistance matters more here than board area and a 2220 is the most crack-prone package there is. 100V also almost eliminates DC bias loss at 8.8V, where the previous 25V 1206 part lost roughly half its capacitance. Pair gives 9.4uF nominal, about 8.9uF at 8.8V bias and roughly 6.3uF at the -10% tolerance and -22% X7S temperature corner, against the 7.5uF from the LTC3639 single-cycle step equation COUT > (L/2)(IPEAK/VOUT)^2 x 100 at the 230mA IPEAK that ISET floating gives; the corner case only widens that step from 1.0% to 1.2% of VOUT, which the 800mV VCollector headroom absorbs. MPN_ALT is the TDK CGA equivalent, which was out of stock when this was chosen

TVS 12V standoff 600W unidirectional DO-214AA SMB AEC-Q101, VBR 13.3V min, VC 19.9V at 30.2A, IR 1uA max at VRWM, -55 to +150C TJ - 8V8 rail clamp. NOT A ZENER: the D_Zener symbol is only the schematic shape, a zener of the same voltage has orders of magnitude less surge capability and must not be substituted. Cathode (pin 1) to +8V8, anode to GND. THE STANDOFF IS SET BY THE OTP RAIL, NOT THE 8.8V RAIL: fitting R604 lifts the rail to 11.1V for OTP programming, so a 10V part (VBR min 11.1V) would conduct hard the moment R604 goes in. 12V leaves 2.2V to VBR min. Its real job is protecting Q201, not the BQ79616 - LDOIN is regulated by the NPNB loop so it stays at 6V whatever the rail does, but without the clamp Q201 would dissipate (67-6)V x 25mA = 1.5W in SOT-223 and cook; with it, 0.2W. In a mis-regulation fault it sits at about 1.4W, which an SMB cannot hold indefinitely - it will eventually fail short, collapsing the rail and killing the board safely

FUSE 500mA 125VAC/125VDC fast acting, Littelfuse 470 Series thin-film chip fuse 1206, 0.5455 Ohm cold resistance, 0.0287 A2s nominal melting I2t, interrupting 50A at 125VDC, -55 to +125C, epoxy resin body with Cu/Ni/Sn terminations, Pb-free and halogen-free, body 3.302 x 1.575 x 1.168mm - cell tap protection; one fuse per connector pin, star connected between each tap connector and the shared VC/CB node, so every connector sees exactly one fuse. Continuous duty is 105mA balance current on the middle taps and up to 180mA on the top and bottom taps, which also carry the whole board supply, so worst case is 36% of rating at 6S low state of charge. The +125C rating matches the Datamate connectors and the BQ79616, unlike the +90C Schurter USF. Uses the Littelfuse recommended land (1.185 x 2.05mm pads on a 1.28mm gap), which is NOT the Schurter 1206 land - the two are not drop-in interchangeable

FUSE 500mA 125VAC/125VDC fast acting, Littelfuse 470 Series thin-film chip fuse 1206, 0.5455 Ohm cold resistance, 0.0287 A2s nominal melting I2t, interrupting 50A at 125VDC, -55 to +125C, epoxy resin body with Cu/Ni/Sn terminations, Pb-free and halogen-free - 8V8 rail fuse, same part as the 51 cell tap fuses. Carries only the BQ79616 LDOIN supply: 11.6mA IACT(IDLE) max, about 25mA with daisy-chain broadcast, ADC, balancing and open-wire test all active, 20mA startup inrush - 5% of nameplate, so no wear-out concern. Drops 14mV at 25mA against the 800mV budget between the 8.80V rail and the 8V minimum TI require at the Q201 collector. CLEARS THE HARD SHORT ONLY: if the LTC3639 high side switch fails short the loop is R601 4R7 + L601 1.65R DCR + this fuse + the top and bottom tap fuses, about 8 Ohm, so 6.7A at 16S and this opens in roughly 640us. It can NOT clear a mis-regulation fault - the LTC3639 current limits at 100mA, which is 20% of rating and never opens a fuse. D601 covers that case
